item.title: See what drifted
item.description: Run this on the new machine: admin diff On a machine that matches its repo: (stdout) No drift: the machine matches /home/admin/arch. After installing htop and dropping a sysctl file into /etc by hand: (stdout) Drift (as the aconfmgr lines that would describe it): AddPackage htop # Interactive process viewer CopyFile /etc/sysctl.d/99-swappiness.conf Each line is what aconfmgr would have to add to the configuration to describe the machine as it is.

item.title: Save and apply
item.description: Every line of drift has two possible fixes: change the repo to match the machine, or change the machine to match the repo. admin save and admin apply are the two. Change the repo: admin save When the drift is something you meant, record it: Run this on the new machine: admin save (stdout) Wrote /home/admin/arch/aconfmgr/99-unsorted.sh. Move what you meant into a numbered file, delete the rest (and 'admin apply' to undo it), then commit.

item.title: Upgrade
item.description: Untested admin upgrade has not yet been run by the test VM, which installs from the current repositories and has nothing to upgrade. Run this on the new machine: admin upgrade One command for the thing you will do most often, in an order worth not having to remember: Refuse to start if admin diff reports drift. Upgrading a machine you cannot describe makes it harder to describe. admin save or admin apply first.

item.title: Snapshots
item.description: setup disk made @snapshots for exactly this. setup install configured snapper to keep snapshots of / (the @ subvolume) there, and installed snap-pac, whose pacman hooks take one snapshot before every transaction and one after: Run this on the new machine: sudo snapper list (stdout) # | Type | Pre # | Date | User | Cleanup | Description | Userdata --+--------+-------+--------------------------+------+---------+---------------------------+--------- 0 | single | | | root | | current | 1 | pre | | Mon Oct 26 05:22:11 2026 | root | number | pacman -S --noconfirm vim | 2 | post | 1 | Mon Oct 26 05:22:14 2026 | root | number | vim | The configuration is in the host repo, at etc/snapper/configs/root:
